findings.highlight: their starring member plus president
findings.evidenceJa: 演出兼座長と、脚本兼主演女優のコンビが有名
findings.explanation: The troupe is famous for a pair consisting of its director/troupe leader and its playwright/leading actress. The English turns the first person's production roles into 'starring member plus president,' changing the division of artistic labor that defines the troupe.
findings.japanese:
「メンバー数は他と比べて圧倒的に少ないけど、
演出兼座長と、脚本兼主演女優のコンビが有名…らしい」
findings.todokanai: "The number of members they have is much less than any other club's, but they have the combination of their starring member plus president, along with their scripter plus leading actress… or so it seems."

findings.highlight: In the first segment of that DVD, during the credits section of that amazing play that took place three years ago.
findings.evidenceJa:
あのＤＶＤの１トラック目。
絶賛の嵐の中幕を閉じた、
三年前の舞台の中で。
findings.explanation: The Japanese says the performance ended amid great acclaim; the English describes the credits section ending.
findings.japanese:
あのＤＶＤの１トラック目。
絶賛の嵐の中幕を閉じた、
三年前の舞台の中で。
findings.todokanai: In the first segment of that DVD, during the credits section of that amazing play that took place three years ago.

findings.highlight: when he's still trying to memorize his lines
findings.evidenceJa: ホン読みの段階でそこまで求めなくても
findings.explanation: This is the script-reading or table-read stage, when another member argues that Chiaki need not demand so much yet. The English invents an actor who is still memorizing lines, replacing the production stage that motivates the objection.
findings.japanese: 「ホン読みの段階でそこまで求めなくても…」
findings.todokanai: "Please don't be so harsh when he's still trying to memorize his lines…"

findings.highlight: He didn't use any emotion
findings.evidenceJa: 読み込んでこなかったの丸わかり
findings.explanation: Chiaki says it is obvious the actor did not study or read the part deeply enough and therefore does not understand the character. The English changes her diagnosis to a lack of emotion, losing the exact standard by which the obsessive actress judges him unfit.
findings.japanese:
「駄目。あいつ“彼”を全然わかってない。
読み込んでこなかったの丸わかり。
…今度の舞台もあたし一人でやる」
findings.todokanai: "No, that person doesn't understand 'him' at all. He didn't use any emotion. …I might as well solo this play as well."

findings.highlight: because you're terrible at picking people
findings.evidenceJa: 座長が顔で選ぶからでしょ
findings.explanation: Chiaki says the problem is that the troupe leader chooses recruits by their faces—because they are good-looking. The English reduces this to generic bad judgment and removes both the joke and the stated reason the male actors lack substance.
findings.japanese:
「座長が顔で選ぶからでしょ。
もうちょっと骨のある奴連れてきてよ」
findings.todokanai: "Isn't that because you're terrible at picking people, President? Why don't you find someone more useful?"

findings.highlight: this should still be "the usual Chiaki."
findings.evidenceJa: ただの『いつもと違う千晶』だったのに
findings.explanation: Without the preceding hour's revelation, Haruki could have dismissed what he saw as merely 'Chiaki acting different from usual.' The English calls it the usual Chiaki, reversing the contrast on which his attempt to normalize her behavior depends.
findings.japanese:
…さっきまでの一時間さえなければ、
ただの『いつもと違う千晶』だったのに。
findings.todokanai: …If it wasn't for what I've seen in the last hour, this should still be "the usual Chiaki."

findings.highlight: The way she's seeing right through me is very painful
findings.evidenceJa: なんて、穿った見方をするのが辛い
findings.explanation: What hurts Haruki is having to take such a cynical, suspicious interpretation of Chiaki's words. The English instead says Chiaki is seeing through him, reversing the perceiver and replacing his guilt about mistrusting her with exposure anxiety.
findings.japanese: なんて、穿った見方をするのが辛い。
findings.todokanai: The way she's seeing right through me is very painful.

findings.highlight: it was actually you putting on a one-man-show again
findings.evidenceJa: 実は、一芝居打っていたのはこいつじゃなくて…
findings.explanation: Haruki desperately entertains the possibility that the person who staged the deception was not Chiaki, before the thought is interrupted. The English says it actually was her putting on another show, reversing the explicit negation and destroying the momentary hope that her present emotion might be genuine.
findings.japanese:
もしかしたら、今まで俺の見たもの全てが幻で、
実は、一芝居打っていたのはこいつじゃなくて…
findings.todokanai: Don't tell me that what I just saw was simply an illusion, that it was actually you putting on a one-man-show again…

findings.highlight: you should confirm it again
findings.evidenceJa: やっぱ再確認したわ
findings.explanation: Takeya says that what he has just seen has reconfirmed his own judgment about Haruki and Chiaki. The English turns this into advice that Haruki should perform another confirmation, changing both subject and speech act.
findings.japanese: 「春希…やっぱ再確認したわ」
findings.todokanai: "Haruki… you should confirm it again."

findings.highlight: the woman in my arms whom I'm supposed to understand very well
findings.evidenceJa: 俺のよき理解者だったはずの女
findings.explanation: Chiaki was supposed to be the woman who understood Haruki well; he now finds her incomprehensible, which makes Takeya's warning suddenly persuasive. The English says Haruki was supposed to understand her, reversing the relationship whose collapse terrifies him.
findings.japanese:
武也の言葉がするりと納得できるくらい、
今、腕の中にいる、俺のよき理解者だったはずの女が
まるで理解できない。
findings.todokanai: I'm suddenly incapable of understanding the woman in my arms whom I'm supposed to understand very well whatsoever, as if I've immediately accepted Takeya's words.

findings.highlight: Yuutsuru
findings.evidenceJa: 『夕鶴』
findings.explanation: Chiaki names Junji Kinoshita's canonical play The Twilight Crane, whose crane-wife story immediately structures the following transformation image. Leaving the title as an unexplained romanization prevents an English reader from recognizing the work or the deliberate allusion.
findings.japanese:
「…『夕鶴』。
中学のとき、これで市の最優秀賞取ったんだ」
findings.todokanai: "…Yuutsuru. It won first place in a competition when I was still in middle school."

findings.highlight: took the form of a human girl
findings.evidenceJa: 人間の女の姿を解いてしまった
findings.explanation: Like the crane wife in The Twilight Crane, Chiaki seems to shed or undo her human woman's form and reveal what lies beneath. The English says the crane assumed human form, reversing the transformation at the precise point Haruki sees the familiar Chiaki disappear.
findings.japanese:
あの日助けた鶴が、
人間の女の姿を解いてしまったように。
findings.todokanai: The crane that was saved that day took the form of a human girl.

findings.highlight: you also have yourself to blame for not realizing it
findings.evidenceJa: 気づかなかった自分を責めても仕方ないよ
findings.explanation: Chiaki says Haruki may blame her for deceiving him, but there is no point blaming himself for failing to notice. The English tells him that he also has himself to blame, reversing her coldly consoling logic and making her assign guilt she explicitly dismisses.
findings.japanese:
「騙したあたしを責めるのはともかく、
気づかなかった自分を責めても仕方ないよ？」
findings.todokanai: "I can't question the fact that I'm at fault for deceiving you, but you also have yourself to blame for not realizing it as well, you know?"

findings.highlight: In this situation so treacherous it's sending chills up my spine, Chiaki's words, demeanor and breaths envelop me in warmth as usual.
findings.evidenceJa:
寒気がするほどの空々しい状況なのに、
やっぱり千晶の言葉と態度と息遣いは、
いつも通り、優しく俺を包み込む。
findings.explanation: Haruki calls the situation hollow and farcical; the English calls it treacherous.
findings.japanese:
寒気がするほどの空々しい状況なのに、
やっぱり千晶の言葉と態度と息遣いは、
いつも通り、優しく俺を包み込む。
findings.todokanai: In this situation so treacherous it's sending chills up my spine, Chiaki's words, demeanor and breaths envelop me in warmth as usual.

findings.highlight: "You commute by train, Haruki, while I commute by bike. You take work at school seriously, while I skip classes all the time. You do your best at studying, while I do my best at after-school activities."
findings.evidenceJa:
「電車通学の春希と、自転車通学のあたし。
学校行事を仕切る春希と、ことごとくサボるあたし。
授業中に頑張る春希と、放課後にしか出てこないあたし」
findings.explanation: Chiaki says the real version of her appeared only after school; the English says she did her best at after-school activities.
findings.japanese:
「電車通学の春希と、自転車通学のあたし。
学校行事を仕切る春希と、ことごとくサボるあたし。
授業中に頑張る春希と、放課後にしか出てこないあたし」
findings.todokanai: "You commute by train, Haruki, while I commute by bike. You take work at school seriously, while I skip classes all the time. You do your best at studying, while I do my best at after-school activities."

findings.highlight: because our performance came directly after yours ended
findings.evidenceJa: 自分の舞台が終わった直後だったから、感傷的になってたんだろ
findings.explanation: Haruki suggests Chiaki became sentimental because her own stage performance had just ended. The English invents a sequence in which the trio's performance came after hers and makes that scheduling relation the cause, replacing his simple explanation of her emotional susceptibility.
findings.japanese:
「自分の舞台が終わった直後だったから、
感傷的になってたんだろ…」
findings.todokanai: "It's natural that you'd feel sad because our performance came directly after yours ended, right..?"

findings.highlight: make both of them feel attracted to you
findings.evidenceJa: 三人をまとめる…そして二人を引っかき回すあんたの力
findings.explanation: Chiaki credits Haruki's power both to bind the trio together and to throw the two women into turmoil, the destructive contradiction that made the stage compelling. The English turns the second force into merely making both women attracted to him, flattening her diagnosis of the trio's drama.
findings.japanese:
「あのステージがあそこまでみんなを惹きつけたのは、
演奏はたどたどしくても、三人をまとめる…
そして二人を引っかき回すあんたの力だったんだって」
findings.todokanai: "Despite the fact that your performance was rather awkward, it was as fascinating as it was because the three of you came together… As well as the fact that you've managed to make both of them feel attracted to you."

findings.highlight: a mysterious close friend who does things mindlessly
findings.evidenceJa: 気のおけない謎の親友
findings.explanation: 気のおけない describes a close friend around whom one need not be guarded or reserved. The English treats it as mindlessness, replacing the ease and intimacy of one of Chiaki's carefully constructed roles with an unrelated behavioral defect.
findings.japanese:
あるときは友達以上恋人未満のゼミ仲間。
あるときは気のおけない謎の親友
findings.todokanai: She's someone from my seminars who's at times more than a friend, but not quite a girlfriend. Other times, she's a mysterious close friend who does things mindlessly.

findings.highlight: made my feelings toward you even clearer
findings.evidenceJa: あんたの呪いの言葉が、あたしの引き出しをまた満たしてくれる
findings.explanation: Chiaki says Haruki's anguished words are filling her drawers—her store or repertoire of material—as an actress. The English says they clarify her feelings, erasing the horrifying double register in which genuine love and predatory artistic collection remain inseparable.
findings.japanese:
「あぁ…愛しい。
あんたの呪いの言葉が、
あたしの引き出しをまた満たしてくれる」
findings.todokanai: "Ahh… I'm loving this. Your accursed words made my feelings toward you even clearer."

findings.highlight: There's no one else who loves you as much as I do
findings.evidenceJa: あたしほどあんたをわかってる人間は他にいないよ
findings.explanation: Chiaki claims that no other human being understands Haruki as well as she does. The English repeats that nobody loves him as much, losing the uniquely disturbing claim validated by how thoroughly she has studied, imitated, and manipulated him.
findings.japanese:
「ううん、真剣。
あたし、春希のこと愛してる。
あたしほどあんたをわかってる人間は他にいないよ？」
findings.todokanai: "No, I'm serious. I really do love you, Haruki. There's no one else who loves you as much as I do in this world, you know?"
